The new Prem season presented both sides with the opportunity to move on from their respective disappointing ends to the last campaign, with Quins finishing down in ninth and Bath's hopes of defending their title ending in a surprise home play-off defeat to a rejuvenated Exeter Chiefs.

Bath took the lead during the game's first spell of sustained pressure in the 12th minute. When Quins stopped the initial line-out catch and drive, Bath number eight Du Preez powered over to ensure a try-scoring start after his move from Sale.

But the hosts hit back through a mix of good fortune and quick-thinking from scrum-half Porter. As Quins lost control of the ball on their own line-out, the pacy Porter picked up the loose ball and raced away to score.

Winger Cokanasiga grabbed Bath's second after sprinting through a gaping gap in the Quins defence following a breakdown and Finn Russell's second conversion made it 14-5 after 20 minutes.

Back came Quins again as Oscar Beard won the aerial contest when Bath tried a cross-field kick and fed debutant fly-half Connor Slevin on the wing, and the man standing in for the injured Marcus Smith passed back inside to England back rower Cunningham-South to cross the whitewash.

Then came the early try-of-the-season contender from Carreras, who stood in Green's passing lane just inside his own 22, before prodding his boot out to intercept and expertly gather the loose ball to score.

Bath showed the grit to go with the glamour as their pack splintered the Quins forwards in first-half added time with hooker Frost the beneficiary. Russell made it four kicks from four to put Bath 28-10 up at half-time.

Delgado crossed from close range and Slevin slotted his first conversion after 45 minutes but the home side were reduced to 14 men when replacement hooker Sam Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Beno Obano just three minutes after coming on.

Bath failed to add to their advantage during Riley's time off the pitch but did grab a fifth try with another maul after 71 minutes and this time it was replacement second row Richards who was the scorer.

Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan speaking to BBC Radio Somerset:

"I thought we started really well. I think we managed the first half really well and to go into the changing room up, away from home, in your first league game, that's something we were really happy about.

"We stuck to our DNA, we were tough to beat and ultimately we've got to be happy with that performance. Loads of things to work on but we'll take an away win in round one. We had loads of opportunities.

"Importantly we didn't give them a bonus because one point is the biggest and smallest margin as who knows what will happen at the back end with points difference."

[On Carreras' try] "That was pure magic. He's been on fire and I'm so glad for him. That might be the try of the season in round one. The kick, the regather, the pace, I loved that moment and it was certainly the moment of the game."

[On Sam Underhill injury] "It looks like a bicep injury and he might be out for some time."

Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore said:

"I'm really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half.

"We had some massive defensive sets on our goal line, which we withstood.

"I'm frustrated that we created a lot of line breaks but we panicked a little bit at the end of them and turned over far too much ball which released pressure off Bath."

fullText:

Tries: Wade 2, Jordan, Kok Cons: Connon, Henry 2

James Pater and Tommy Freeman ran in hat-tricks as Northampton Saints kicked off their title defence with a comfortable 59-26 win over new-look Newcastle Red Bulls at Franklin's Gardens.

Just three months after securing a second Prem title against Exeter Chiefs at Allianz Stadium, Saints were dominant against a much-changed Red Bulls side who have welcomed 25 new players through the door this summer.

Three tries each for Pater and Freeman and one each for George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme delivered an emphatic scoreline as Saints, brilliantly conducted by fly-half Fin Smith, ran in nine tries.

Yet for all that the scoreline delivered another defeat for Newcastle they still scored four tries and came away with a losing bonus point as they hope that, for the first time in five seasons, they may not be destined for bottom place in the Prem.

Pater went over twice inside the first 15 minutes with Hendy, Freeman and Coles all following him in during a first period Northampton bossed.

But two tries from Christian Wade which were both converted - with the first a brilliant end-to-end and side-to-side score which had levelled matters early - showed Newcastle will cause problems for plenty of teams this season.

If those were the positives, two yellow cards were the balancers for the visitors. A first for a trip by Harrison Obatoyinbo and the second for a no-hands tackle under the sticks by Pouri Rakete-Stones hampered their defensive effort.

Those mistakes allowed Saints to stretch clear in the second period.

Throughout the 80 minutes the visitors had no real answer to the power and pace of Henry Pollock, who celebrated his new £400,000 contract extension not only with an eye-catching braided hairstyle but a performance which justified it all.

Pollock was not alone in hitting the ground running with Smith superb and Freeman and Pater ruthless.

Freeman completed his hat-trick with two second-half tries either side of Cam Jordan's first for Newcastle, after signing from Gloucester in the summer.

Sleightholme pounced just seconds after coming on as a substitute and the impressive Pater rounded off the win with his own hat-trick.

However, the impressively mobile Werner Kok scored a consolation late on to ensure Newcastle left with a bonus point to their name.

Northampton Saints' Tommy Freeman told BBC Radio Northampton:

"Good start and lots of points on the board which good to see but I think there is loads 

"Our set piece we need to tighten up a bit on that first phase. Defensively we were caught a bit tight, but credit to Newcastle for stressing us in those areas but we would like to see better movement.

"It is always a challenge and going back-to-back [titles] is not done by many teams. There is a reason for that but we will be looking to take each week as it comes and keep putting our DNA on the pitch."

Newcastle head coach Dan McFarland told BBC Radio Newcastle:

"We put a lot of good stuff out there but we were tested today by a really, really good team. We know where we stand now and where we've got to work. We have a long jounrey ahead of us and that was the first step.

"It was a fantastic score when we had a length of the field try and that was really us and we also had a lot of defensive sets where we had showed really good scramble and stopped them from scoring.

"But the game is up and down. We had that yellow card and then we had three tries which were scored during that yellow, and the try just before half-time was a real killer.

"Maybe we left a couple of tries out there but there is plenty in that that we will take away and see as a real positive."

title: Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final
description: Warrington Wolves reach their first Super League Grand Final in eight years with a thrilling victory against Leeds Rhinos.
fullText:
Betfred Super League play-off semi-final

Tries: Hall, Connor Goals: Connor 2

Tries: Bentley, Yates Goals: Irwin 3

Warrington Wolves have reached their first Super League Grand Final in eight years with a thrilling victory against Leeds Rhinos at AMT Headingley Stadium.

In a tense and topsy-turvy semi-final the sides traded two first-half tries each and were locked at 12-12 at the break, before the Wolves were awarded a contentious penalty which was slotted nervelessly by 18-year-old Ewan Irwin to nudge them ahead.

Half-back Jake Connor scored 10 points for an injury-depleted Rhinos, including a first-half try which he inventively created in midfield, and attempted a goal-kick from 62 metres out with the final play of the game but the ball landed short of the sticks.

The Wolves will face the winners of either Wigan Warriors or Wakefield Trinity in the showpiece final at Old Trafford next Saturday, as they stand just one win away from a first league title since 1955.

Live text coverage of the first Super League semi-final

Old hands or new blood? Wigan & Wakefield vie to reach Grand Final

Leeds limped into the semi-final missing a number of key players including the league's top try-scorer Maika Sivo, captain Ash Handley, and Man of Steel nominee Lachie Miller.

The Rhinos were dealt with a further injury blow moments before kick-off when Chris Hankinson pulled up in the warm-up and had to be replaced by Ned McCormack in the starting line-up.

Warrington breached Leeds' inexperienced backline after five minutes as England captain George Williams' pinpoint kick was met by Matty Ashton, who helped find former Rhino James Bentley to slide over for an early score.

Brodie Croft's cut-out pass found Ryan Hall to score his 358th career try to draw level with former Wakefield legend Neil Fox in the all-time scorers list, as Connor nailed the extras from touch to drag Leeds level.

Connor was then involved at the other end of the field, teaming up with young full-back Fergie McCormack to usher Albert Hopoate into touch as he threatened to score and moments later Arron Lindop collided with team-mate Hopoate as the Wolves again squandered a certain four points.

Leeds made the Wolves pay soon later as they raced down field. A delicate kick over the top from Connor bounced kindly for McCormack, and once Kallum Watkins found Connor he was not to be denied by Ashton's scrambling defending, using his momentum to spin and crash down.

Moments before the break, prop Luke Yates pirouetted elegantly past Cooper Jenkins to slide in next to the sticks as Irwin levelled the scores with the boot as half-time approached.

The game's decisive moment came after the break when James McDonnell was adjudged to have challenged Williams off the ball under a high ball and Irwin stepped up to the tee to notch Warrington two points in front.

A charge down from Keenan Palasia near his own line kept Leeds in the fight but a great tackle from Bentley forced a knock-on as both defences were on top in the second period.

Connor's sensational 40/20 with two minutes remaining ultimately was in vain as Palasia's ball-carrying arm had already hit the floor in the build-up.

A block off the ball gave Connor the chance to be the hero and force the game into golden point but, at the wire, he was unable to find the distance required and Williams kicked the ball into touch to the relief of the travelling supporters.

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur said:

"I've not whinged or complained the whole time I've been here. I'm extremely proud of our team and our club and players.

"I don't know what more we could have really done. We got a couple of bits and pieces wrong but so did they. It just would have been really nice if the game was decided by an individual or a piece of skill.

"We're talking about a field goal or something like that rather than a soft penalty to decide such a big game. It is a soft penalty.

"Ned got escorted four or five times tonight on kicks and I wasn't expecting penalties for them. But that's a soft penalty to decide such a big game."

Warrington Wolves captain George Williams told BBC Radio Merseyside:

"Nerve-wracking, mad game, just pleased we've came through the other side.

"Credit to Leeds, they gave it a good crack. They've been a great team all year but we rode the waves and the main thing is we're through to the big dance next week.

"They were probably dominant for the first 20 [minutes], we came home strong in the back end [of the first half]. It's no good for the nerves but sometimes it's better when you're out there, you can do something about it."

[On earning the match-winning penalty] "People think it might be a bit controversial but I was chasing the ball and I got a little nudge. I was off balance and nowadays, with the escorts, they give them. Luckily, it went to us and that was the game."

title: Rodri believes in Man City's 'innocence'
description: Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri believes the club are innocent of any financial wrongdoing and will trust them unless they are proved otherwise.
fullText:
Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri believes the club are innocent of any financial wrongdoing and will continue to trust them unless they are proved otherwise.

City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching by the Premier League, although they are set to appeal.

Speaking at a news conference before Spain's Uefa Nations League match against England at Wembley the 30-year-old, who joined Barcelona in August, backed City's stance.

"They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong and we believe in that," Rodri said.

"Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence."

City were cleared of separate financial fair play charges by the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020, having initially been given a two-year ban from European competitions by Uefa.

Rodri cited the case as a reason for the confidence of the club's players.

"We had the example of 2020 that the process was the same and at the end nothing happened," he explained.

"We have faced something similar, we had a similar judicial process. Different accusation but similar process.

"There as well in the first instance we were found guilty, but we believed in the club and the innocence that the club maintained and in the end we ended up acquitted.

"So, I believe in the justice system, and I believe in the innocence of the club."

The club won eight trophies in the period covered by the Premier League case, including three league titles, three League Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

Rodri dismissed talk of City being stripped of some of the titles they won as part of any punishment against the club.

"What we did, they cannot take out of us," he added.

"It's something that is not paid by money. It's paid with effort, with the damage, with, you know, being shoulder to shoulder every day.

"I can tell you that everything was deserved, and I'm glad that I could live one of the best eras of English football in here."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged people to "study" the independent commission's report in "some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions" on the charges facing Manchester City.

"I would have to look at the report of the independent commission, and people shouldn't jump to those kinds of conclusions," Burnham told ITV Granada.

"I know this has been a long process between the club and the Premier League. I think it has been quite a contested process.

"So I don't think it's as simple as jumping to conclusions. I think we would all need to study the independent commission's report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions."
